tim_customer: hey team, integrating the starter-kit right now — getting a mix of 401 then a flurry of 429s after a token rotate. app is single-process, node sdk v1.3.2.

sara_cs: hi @tim_customer — sorry about that. can you paste the exact error lines from the SDK logs? especially the Authorization header and the timestamp around the 401 -> 429 transition.

 tim_customer: here are the relevant lines: 
```
[2026-03-21T15:02:10.123Z] request start POST /v1/generate headers={Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, x-client-id: starter-kit, concurrency:1}
[2026-03-21T15:02:10.345Z] response 401 body={"error":"invalid_token"}
[2026-03-21T15:02:12.001Z] token rotated, new token fetched
[2026-03-21T15:02:12.250Z] request start POST /v1/generate headers={Authorization: Bearer <new>, x-client-id: starter-kit}
[2026-03-21T15:02:12.500Z] response 429 body={"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","limit":"sandbox_fanout"}
```

eli_devx: The pattern looks like: token rotation triggers a short window where many connections are re-established and hit the sandbox fanout cap. Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) add jittered backoff on token refresh and 2) limit parallel warmup requests during rotation.

eli_devx: e.g. in node: 
```
const client = new RedwoodSDK({ maxConcurrency: 2, retry: { maxAttempts: 6, baseDelayMs: 300, jitter: true } });
// hold warmup calls behind a gate while token refreshes
```

ben_infra: fwiw, our edge proxy does connection pooling that can send requests with stale creds if token swap races with keepalive reuse. If you rotate tokens very frequently, you can see 401 then a rapid burst of retries that triggers 429.

ben_infra: temporary workaround: increase token overlap window (server-side) or perform a graceful two-step rotation: mark old token as draining for 30s before full revoke. i'll check if your account is on aggressive rotation policy.

ops_monitor: @sara_cs @tim_customer saw a sandbox_fanout spike at 15:02:12 matching the log — looks like you exhausted the per-minute fanout slot during the token warmup. we can bump the fanout limit for the onboarding window if you need immediate headroom.

sara_cs: thanks everyone. @tim_customer — can you confirm how often your app rotates tokens? hourly? on every restart? also do you do warmup bursts on deploy?

 tim_customer: rotation is on restart only for now, but we added a background refresh that runs every 45s while testing — oops. warmup runs 10 parallel requests after boot.

sara_cs: ok that explains it. two action items: 1) disable frequent refresh during initial onboarding and switch to client-side exponential backoff w/ jitter (eli's snippet), 2) i'll request a temporary fanout bump for 1 hour while you finish integration. can we also hop on a 20m screen share in 30m?

 tim_customer: yep available. thanks — i'll flip the refresh off and rerun.

deploy-bot: deploy: starter-kit/integration @tim_customer started at 2026-03-21T15:23:00Z — 1 instance updated :rocket:

eli_devx: quick tip for the SDK: if you expect token rotation, expose a `tokenProvider` callback so the client always pulls fresh header per request instead of caching across sockets. prevents reuse races.

ops_monitor: fanout bump scheduled for +60m starting 2026-03-21T15:30:00Z. monitoring alerts will be relaxed for that window.

sara_cs: great. i'll send calendar invite for the 30m check-in. please paste results from the rerun in this thread. :thumbsup:
